title: Beyond Static Intelligence: Evaluating Continual Learning — Parth Asawa, UC Berkeley
talk_summary: Parth Asawa argues that standard LLM benchmarks evaluate models statelessly, so they cannot measure continual learning, and proposes Continual Learning Bench with headroom, shared structure, and a learning signal. He introduces a 'gain' metric (stateful minus stateless reward) to separate base model strength from actual learning, and reports that vanilla in-context learning beat fancier context-management systems on reward and Pareto frontiers.

takeaways.technique: Stateful-vs-stateless gain metric for agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Run each system twice over a task sequence: once with state carried across instances, once resetting between every instance; the per-instance difference isolates how much prior experience helped versus base model strength.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Gain refers to the difference between stateful reward and stateless reward.
takeaways.numbers: Vanilla in-context learning topped the leaderboard on reward and on reward-vs-cost and gain-vs-cost Pareto frontiers; more expensive context-management systems performed 'a lot poorly' by comparison.

takeaways.technique: Prefer plain in-context experience over elaborate context-management machinery
takeaways.what_they_do: Benchmarked vanilla in-context learning against notepad/external-memory style context managers on tasks requiring real adaptation; the simple approach won on reward and cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these more expensive context management systems perform a lot poorly compared to just vanilla in context learning
takeaways.numbers: Vanilla ICL topped aggregate reward and both Pareto frontiers (reward vs cost, gain vs cost).

takeaways.technique: Design for concept drift: expire stale memory explicitly
takeaways.what_they_do: Injects database migrations (dropped/renamed columns, format changes) into task sequences to test whether agents discard stale experience and update priors; observed failures where agents either ignored relevant old schema or reverted to stale predictions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it might struggle in its ability to detect and discard stale experience and simultaneously update from new experience

takeaways.technique: Benchmark tasks need headroom, shared structure, and a learning signal
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues chained independent benchmarks cannot measure learning because instances share no latent structure and offer no feedback signal; good continual-learning tasks require online adaptation, shared structure across instances, and reward/error/textual feedback.
takeaways.evidence_quote: benchmark instances are in traditional language model evaluation are designed to be independent

takeaways.technique: Diagnose failures as stability vs plasticity
takeaways.what_they_do: Classifies continual-learning failure modes into stability failures (not retaining prior information, e.g. reverting to an earlier wrong prediction) and plasticity failures (not updating priors from new evidence, e.g. dismissing a schema as irrelevant when it applies).
takeaways.evidence_quote: most failure modes in continual learning fall on one side of the stability plasticity trade-off
